title: Swap a hand-written fake for gMock
summary: FakeMailer becomes MOCK_METHOD and EXPECT_CALL. Times(2) with one WillOnce leaves the second call without an action.

turns.user: FakeMailer in notifier_test counts its own calls and it's annoying. just use gmock

assistant.body: Great idea. FakeMailer becomes MockMailer. MOCK_METHOD takes the return type, the name, the parameters in parentheses, and the qualifiers. Expectations are declared up front with EXPECT_CALL, and gMock checks the count and the arguments when the mock is destroyed. So the ASSERT on sent goes away.

turns.user: passes but RetriesOnceOnFailure prints Too few actions specified in EXPECT_CALL(mailer, send(_, _))...

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was not accurate. Times(2) has only one WillOnce, so the second call has no action and gMock returns the default for bool, which is false. The test passed by accident. WillRepeatedly covers every call after the first.

turns.user: also want a test that it stops sending once the retry works

assistant.body: Two WillOnce in a row fix the count at exactly two, without writing Times. A third call fails the test on the spot.
